title.value: HOTA: Hamiltonian framework for Optimal Transport Advection

TLDR.value: A new method based on Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation that solves generalized Schrödinger bridge problem.

abstract.value: Optimal transport (OT) has become a natural framework for guiding the probability flows. Yet, the majority of recent generative models assume trivial geometry (e.g., Euclidean) and rely on strong density-estimation assumptions, yielding trajectories that do not respect the true principles of optimality in the underlying manifold. We present Hamiltonian Optimal Transport Advection (HOTA), a Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman based method that tackles the dual dynamical OT problem explicitly through Kantorovich potentials, enabling efficient and scalable trajectory optimization. Our approach effectively evades the need for explicit density modeling, performing even when the cost functionals are non-smooth. Empirically, HOTA outperforms all baselines in standard benchmarks, as well as in custom datasets with non-differentiable costs, both in terms of feasibility and optimality.

primary_area.value: probabilistic methods (Bayesian methods, variational inference, sampling, UQ, etc.)
